name: Highly Elliptical Orbit
story: Not an altitude, a shape. A long ellipse with a low perigee (close to Earth) and a very high apogee (sometimes higher than GEO). The orbiter spends most of its time near apogee, hanging slowly over high latitudes — the trick Soviet engineers used to get continuous comms over Russia's polar regions where a GEO satellite over the equator is too low on the horizon to see. Used today for missile-warning, deep-space tracking, and high-latitude broadband.
comparison: Apogee can reach 1/8th of the way to the Moon; perigee can graze the top of LEO. The orbiter sprints near Earth and crawls at the top.
